subject: physics
body: A uniform disc of mass $M$ and radius $R$ rotates about an axis through its centre, perpendicular to its plane. What is its moment of inertia about this axis?

explanation.body: Integrating $r^2\,dm$ over the disc gives $I=\frac{1}{2}MR^2$. The $\frac{2}{5}MR^2$ result belongs to a solid sphere about a diameter, and $MR^2$ to a thin ring.

subject: physics
body: A solid sphere of mass $2\ \text{kg}$ and radius $0.1\ \text{m}$ rotates about a diameter. Find its moment of inertia, in $\text{kg}\,\text{m}^2$.

explanation.body: For a solid sphere about a diameter, $I=\frac{2}{5}MR^2=\frac{2}{5}(2)(0.1)^2=0.008\ \text{kg}\,\text{m}^2$.

subject: physics
body: A disc spins freely at angular speed $\omega$ about its central axis. A ring of the same mass and radius is gently lowered onto it, coaxially, and the two rotate together. The new angular speed is:

explanation.body: No external torque acts, so angular momentum is conserved. Initially $L=\frac{1}{2}MR^2\omega$. Afterwards $I=\frac{1}{2}MR^2+MR^2=\frac{3}{2}MR^2$, so $\omega'=\frac{\frac{1}{2}}{\frac{3}{2}}\omega=\frac{\omega}{3}$.

subject: physics
body: A particle moves along a straight line with $x(t)=3t^2-2t^3$, where $x$ is in metres and $t$ in seconds. At what time, in seconds, is its acceleration zero?

explanation.body: $v=\frac{dx}{dt}=6t-6t^2$ and $a=\frac{dv}{dt}=6-12t$. Setting $a=0$ gives $t=0.5\ \text{s}$.

subject: physics
body: A projectile is launched at $20\ \text{m/s}$ at the angle that maximises range. Taking $g=10\ \text{m/s}^2$ and ignoring air resistance, find the range in metres.

explanation.body: Range is maximum at $45^\circ$, where $R=\frac{u^2}{g}=\frac{20^2}{10}=40\ \text{m}$.

subject: physics
body: A constant force of $10\ \text{N}$ acts on a $2\ \text{kg}$ block, initially at rest on a frictionless surface, along its direction of motion for $5\ \text{m}$. Find the final speed in $\text{m/s}$, to two decimal places.

explanation.body: Work done $=Fd=50\ \text{J}$. By the work–energy theorem $\frac{1}{2}mv^2=50$, so $v=\sqrt{50}\approx7.07\ \text{m/s}$.

subject: physics
body: Capacitors of $3\ \mu\text{F}$ and $6\ \mu\text{F}$ are connected in series. The equivalent capacitance is:

explanation.body: In series, $\frac{1}{C}=\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{6}=\frac{1}{2}$, so $C=2\ \mu\text{F}$. Note the series result is always smaller than the smallest capacitor.

subject: physics
body: Three unequal resistors are connected in series across an ideal battery. Which statements are correct?

options.body: The current is the same through each resistor.
The potential difference is the same across each resistor.
The largest resistor dissipates the most power.
The equivalent resistance is smaller than the smallest resistor.

explanation.body: Series elements share one current, so (a) holds. With $P=I^2R$ and $I$ common, the largest $R$ dissipates most, giving (c). Voltage divides in proportion to resistance, so (b) fails, and series resistances add, so (d) describes a parallel combination.

subject: physics
body: An ideal gas expands isothermally and reversibly. Which statement is correct?

options.body: $\Delta U=0$ and the gas absorbs heat equal to the work it does.
$\Delta U>0$ and no heat is exchanged.
$\Delta U<0$ and the gas releases heat.
$Q=0$ and the work is done at the expense of internal energy.

explanation.body: Internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on temperature, so an isothermal change gives $\Delta U=0$. The first law then reduces to $Q=W$. Option (d) describes an adiabatic expansion instead.

subject: physics
body: A simple pendulum of length $1.0\ \text{m}$ oscillates with small amplitude where $g=9.8\ \text{m/s}^2$. Find its time period in seconds, to two decimal places.

explanation.body: $T=2\pi\sqrt{\frac{L}{g}}=2\pi\sqrt{\frac{1.0}{9.8}}\approx2.01\ \text{s}$. The period is independent of the bob's mass.

subject: physics
body: A body starts from rest and moves with constant acceleration. The ratio of the distance covered in the first second to that covered in the first three seconds is:

explanation.body: With $s=\tfrac12 a t^2$, distances go as $t^2$: $1^2:3^2 = 1:9$.

subject: physics
body: A stone is thrown vertically upward at $15\ \text{m/s}$. Taking $g=10\ \text{m/s}^2$, how long (in seconds) does it take to return to the thrower's hand?

explanation.body: Time up $=u/g=1.5\ \text{s}$; total time is twice that, $3\ \text{s}$.

subject: physics
body: Two cars start from the same point. Car A travels east at $30\ \text{km/h}$, car B north at $40\ \text{km/h}$. After 1 hour the distance between them is:

explanation.body: Perpendicular displacements $30$ and $40$ give $\sqrt{30^2+40^2}=50\ \text{km}$.

subject: physics
body: The velocity–time graph of a particle is a straight line with negative slope that stays above the time axis. During this interval the particle:

explanation.body: Velocity is positive (graph above axis) so motion is forward; slope (acceleration) is negative, so speed decreases.

subject: physics
body: A ball dropped from a height hits the ground in $2\ \text{s}$. From what height, in metres, was it dropped? Take $g=9.8\ \text{m/s}^2$.

subject: physics
body: A projectile is fired with speed $u$ at angle $\theta$. At the highest point of the trajectory its speed is:

explanation.body: The vertical component vanishes at the top; only the horizontal component $u\cos\theta$ remains.

subject: physics
body: Which quantity is always directed towards the centre for a body in uniform circular motion?

explanation.body: Speed is constant, but the velocity direction changes; the centripetal acceleration points to the centre.

subject: physics
body: A net force of $12\ \text{N}$ acts on a $3\ \text{kg}$ body. Find its acceleration in $\text{m/s}^2$.

subject: physics
body: A lift accelerates upward at $2\ \text{m/s}^2$. The apparent weight of a $50\ \text{kg}$ passenger (take $g=10\ \text{m/s}^2$) is:

subject: physics
body: A block of mass $m$ rests on a rough incline of angle $\theta$ without sliding. The friction force on it is:

explanation.body: For equilibrium along the incline, static friction exactly balances the gravitational component $mg\sin\theta$ (it is not at its maximum value here).

subject: physics
body: Two blocks of $2\ \text{kg}$ and $3\ \text{kg}$ are in contact on a frictionless surface. A force of $10\ \text{N}$ pushes the $2\ \text{kg}$ block. The contact force between them is:

explanation.body: System acceleration $=10/5=2\ \text{m/s}^2$. Force on the $3\ \text{kg}$ block $=3\times2=6\ \text{N}$.

subject: physics
body: Newton's third law force pairs always:

explanation.body: Action and reaction act on two different bodies, are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction, so they never cancel on one body.

subject: physics
body: A $0.2\ \text{kg}$ ball moving at $10\ \text{m/s}$ strikes a wall normally and rebounds at $8\ \text{m/s}$. Find the magnitude of the impulse on the ball, in $\text{N s}$.

subject: physics
body: The coefficient of static friction between a box and the floor is $0.4$. The box weighs $50\ \text{N}$. The minimum horizontal force needed to start it moving is:

explanation.body: $f_{\max}=\mu N = 0.4\times50 = 20\ \text{N}$.

subject: physics
body: A force of $10\ \text{N}$ acts on a body but the body does not move. The work done by the force is:

explanation.body: Work $=F\,d\cos\theta$; with zero displacement the work is zero.

subject: physics
body: A $1000\ \text{kg}$ car accelerates from $10\ \text{m/s}$ to $20\ \text{m/s}$. Find the work done on it, in kilojoules.

subject: physics
body: A body of mass $m$ is raised to height $h$ and then allowed to fall freely. Just before it hits the ground its kinetic energy is:

explanation.body: All the potential energy $mgh$ converts to kinetic energy (no losses).

subject: physics
body: A pump raises $600\ \text{kg}$ of water per minute to a height of $10\ \text{m}$. Find its power output in watts. Take $g=10\ \text{m/s}^2$.

subject: physics
body: A spring of force constant $200\ \text{N/m}$ is compressed by $0.1\ \text{m}$. The elastic potential energy stored is:

subject: physics
body: In a perfectly inelastic head-on collision between two bodies, which quantity is always conserved?

explanation.body: Momentum is conserved in any collision; kinetic energy is lost in an inelastic one.

subject: physics
body: The work done by a conservative force over any closed path is:

explanation.body: That path-independence (zero work around a loop) is the defining property of a conservative force.

options.body: equal to the change in kinetic energy

subject: physics
body: The moment of inertia of a thin uniform rod of mass $M$ and length $L$ about an axis through its centre and perpendicular to its length is:

explanation.body: Standard result; about an end it would be $ML^2/3$.

subject: physics
body: A wheel starting from rest reaches $20\ \text{rad/s}$ in $4\ \text{s}$ under constant angular acceleration. Find that angular acceleration in $\text{rad/s}^2$.

explanation.body: $\alpha = \Delta\omega/\Delta t = 20/4 = 5\ \text{rad/s}^2$.

subject: physics
body: A solid sphere and a hollow sphere of the same mass and radius roll down an incline from rest without slipping. Which reaches the bottom first?

explanation.body: Smaller moment of inertia (per $MR^2$) means more of the energy goes into translation, so the solid sphere accelerates faster.

subject: physics
body: A dancer spinning with arms outstretched pulls her arms in. Her angular speed:

explanation.body: With no external torque, angular momentum $I\omega$ is conserved; reducing $I$ increases $\omega$.

subject: physics
body: A torque of $10\ \text{N m}$ acts on a body of moment of inertia $2\ \text{kg m}^2$. Find its angular acceleration in $\text{rad/s}^2$.

explanation.body: $\tau = I\alpha \Rightarrow \alpha = 10/2 = 5\ \text{rad/s}^2$.

subject: physics
body: For a body rolling without slipping, the ratio of rotational kinetic energy to total kinetic energy for a uniform disc is:

explanation.body: Disc: $K_{rot}=\tfrac12 I\omega^2 = \tfrac14 Mv^2$, $K_{trans}=\tfrac12 Mv^2$; ratio $= (\tfrac14)/(\tfrac14+\tfrac12) = 1/3$.

subject: physics
body: The acceleration due to gravity at a height equal to the Earth's radius above the surface is (with $g$ the surface value):

explanation.body: $g\propto 1/r^2$; at $r=2R$ it is $g/4$.

subject: physics
body: The orbital speed of a satellite in a circular orbit close to the Earth's surface is about:

explanation.body: $v=\sqrt{gR}\approx\sqrt{9.8\times6.4\times10^6}\approx7.9\ \text{km/s}$. $11.2\ \text{km/s}$ is the escape speed.

subject: physics
body: A planet's orbital period $T$ and mean orbital radius $r$ obey:

explanation.body: Kepler's third law.

subject: physics
body: The gravitational potential energy of a two-body system is taken as zero when the bodies are:

explanation.body: By convention $U(\infty)=0$, so bound systems have negative potential energy.

options.body: at the centre of the Earth

subject: physics
body: The escape speed from a planet is $v$. If both its mass and radius are doubled, the new escape speed is $kv$. Find $k$.

explanation.body: $v_e=\sqrt{2GM/R}$; doubling both $M$ and $R$ leaves the ratio $M/R$ unchanged, so $k=1$.

subject: physics
body: The weight of a body at the centre of the Earth is:

explanation.body: Gravitational field at the centre of a uniform sphere is zero, so weight is zero (mass is unchanged).

options.body: the same as at the surface

subject: physics
body: In an adiabatic process:

explanation.body: Adiabatic means $Q=0$; the first law then gives $\Delta U = -W$.

options.body: no heat is exchanged with the surroundings

subject: physics
body: A gas absorbs $500\ \text{J}$ of heat and does $200\ \text{J}$ of work on the surroundings. Find the change in its internal energy, in joules.

explanation.body: First law: $\Delta U = Q - W = 500 - 200 = 300\ \text{J}$.

subject: physics
body: A Carnot engine operates between $600\ \text{K}$ and $300\ \text{K}$. Its efficiency is:

subject: physics
body: For an ideal gas, the internal energy depends only on:

explanation.body: Internal energy of an ideal gas is a function of temperature alone.

subject: physics
body: The second law of thermodynamics implies that in any spontaneous process the total entropy of an isolated system:

explanation.body: $\Delta S_{total} \ge 0$, with equality only for a reversible process.

subject: physics
body: The work done by a gas during a process at constant volume is:

explanation.body: $W = \int P\,dV = 0$ when $V$ is constant.

subject: physics
body: For a body in simple harmonic motion, the acceleration is:

explanation.body: $a = -\omega^2 x$: magnitude proportional to displacement, direction towards the equilibrium point.

options.body: directed away from the mean position
directed towards the mean position and proportional to displacement

subject: physics
body: A mass on a spring completes 20 oscillations in $10\ \text{s}$. Find its frequency in hertz.

subject: physics
body: If the length of a simple pendulum is increased four times, its time period:

explanation.body: $T\propto\sqrt{L}$, so $L\to4L$ gives $T\to2T$.

subject: physics
body: In SHM, the kinetic energy equals the potential energy when the displacement from the mean position is:

explanation.body: PE $\propto x^2$, total $\propto A^2$; PE = half total when $x^2 = A^2/2$.

subject: physics
body: The phase difference between displacement and velocity in SHM is:

explanation.body: If $x = A\sin\omega t$ then $v = A\omega\cos\omega t$ — a quarter-cycle ahead.

subject: physics
body: A damped oscillator loses energy over time. Its amplitude:

explanation.body: Damping removes mechanical energy, so the amplitude decays.

subject: physics
body: The electric field inside a hollow charged conducting sphere (no charge inside the cavity) is:

explanation.body: A conductor in electrostatic equilibrium has zero field in its interior and cavity.

subject: physics
body: Two point charges of $+2\ \mu\text{C}$ and $+3\ \mu\text{C}$ are $1\ \text{m}$ apart. Find the magnitude of the force between them, in newtons. Use $k = 9\times10^9\ \text{N m}^2/\text{C}^2$.

subject: physics
body: The work done in moving a charge between two points on the same equipotential surface is:

explanation.body: No potential difference means no work, regardless of the path.

subject: physics
body: The capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor is doubled by:

explanation.body: $C = \varepsilon_0 A / d$, so halving $d$ doubles $C$.

subject: physics
body: A dielectric slab is inserted into an isolated charged capacitor (battery disconnected). The energy stored:

explanation.body: Charge is fixed; $C$ increases so $U = Q^2/2C$ decreases (the slab is pulled in, doing work).

subject: physics
body: Electric field lines:

explanation.body: A crossing point would imply two field directions at once. Electrostatic field lines start on positive and end on negative charges (they are not closed loops).

subject: physics
body: A resistor carries $2\ \text{A}$ when $12\ \text{V}$ is applied across it. Find its resistance in ohms.

subject: physics
body: Three equal resistors $R$ are connected in parallel. The equivalent resistance is:

subject: physics
body: A $60\ \text{W}$ bulb runs on $240\ \text{V}$. Find the current it draws, in amperes.

subject: physics
body: The drift velocity of electrons in a conductor carrying a steady current is typically of the order of:

explanation.body: Drift speed is very small (fractions of a mm/s); the signal, not the electrons, travels near light speed.

subject: physics
body: A battery of emf $\varepsilon$ and internal resistance $r$ delivers maximum power to an external resistor $R$ when:

explanation.body: Maximum power transfer occurs at impedance matching, $R = r$ (efficiency is then $50\%$).

subject: physics
body: The resistance of a metallic wire increases with temperature because:

explanation.body: Hotter lattice ions vibrate more, raising the collision rate and hence resistivity.

options.body: increased lattice vibrations scatter electrons more
the number of free electrons falls sharply

subject: chemistry
body: How many moles are there in $36\ \text{g}$ of water? (Molar mass $= 18\ \text{g/mol}$.)

subject: chemistry
body: Find the number of molecules in $0.5\ \text{mol}$ of CO$_2$. Give the answer as a multiple of $10^{23}$ (i.e. enter the coefficient). Take $N_A = 6.0\times10^{23}$.

explanation.body: $0.5 \times 6.0\times10^{23} = 3.0\times10^{23}$ molecules.

subject: chemistry
body: The percentage by mass of nitrogen in ammonium nitrate, NH$_4$NO$_3$ (molar mass $80\ \text{g/mol}$), is:

explanation.body: Two N atoms $= 28\ \text{g}$ out of $80\ \text{g}$: $28/80 = 35\%$.

subject: chemistry
body: At STP, the volume occupied by $0.25\ \text{mol}$ of an ideal gas is about:

explanation.body: Molar volume at STP $\approx 22.4\ \text{L}$; $0.25 \times 22.4 = 5.6\ \text{L}$.

subject: chemistry
body: In the reaction $2\text{H}_2 + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$, how many grams of water form from $4\ \text{g}$ of H$_2$ reacting with excess O$_2$? (H$_2$: $2\ \text{g/mol}$, H$_2$O: $18\ \text{g/mol}$.)

explanation.body: $4\ \text{g}$ H$_2$ $= 2\ \text{mol}$; this gives $2\ \text{mol}$ H$_2$O $= 36\ \text{g}$.

subject: chemistry
body: Which sample contains the largest number of atoms?

explanation.body: Ozone has 3 atoms per molecule, so $1\ \text{mol}$ O$_3$ $= 3N_A$ atoms — more than the others.

subject: chemistry
body: What is the molarity of a solution made by dissolving $0.2\ \text{mol}$ of NaCl in enough water to make $500\ \text{mL}$ of solution? Answer in mol/L.

explanation.body: $M = 0.2\ \text{mol} / 0.5\ \text{L} = 0.4\ \text{M}$.

subject: chemistry
body: The maximum number of electrons that can occupy the $n=3$ shell is:

subject: chemistry
body: Which set of quantum numbers is not allowed?

explanation.body: $l$ ranges from $0$ to $n-1$, so $l=2$ is impossible for $n=2$.

subject: chemistry
body: The ground-state electronic configuration of a chlorine atom ($Z=17$) is:

explanation.body: 17 electrons fill up to $3p^5$.

subject: chemistry
body: The number of neutrons in an atom of $^{40}_{20}\text{Ca}$ is:

explanation.body: Neutrons $= A - Z = 40 - 20 = 20$.

subject: chemistry
body: According to Bohr's model, the radius of an electron's orbit in a hydrogen atom is proportional to:

explanation.body: Bohr radius $r_n = a_0 n^2$ for hydrogen.

subject: chemistry
body: The shape of a $p$ orbital is:

explanation.body: $p$ orbitals are dumb-bell shaped with a nodal plane through the nucleus.

subject: chemistry
body: Isotopes of an element differ in:

explanation.body: Same $Z$ (protons), different $A$ — i.e. different neutron count.

options.body: number of electrons in the neutral atom

subject: chemistry
body: Across a period from left to right, atomic radius generally:

explanation.body: Nuclear charge rises while the shell stays the same, pulling electrons in.

subject: chemistry
body: Which element has the highest first ionisation energy?

explanation.body: Ionisation energy peaks at the noble gases; Ne has a full shell and small radius.

subject: chemistry
body: The most electronegative element in the periodic table is:

explanation.body: Fluorine has the highest electronegativity (about 4.0 on the Pauling scale).

subject: chemistry
body: Elements in the same group of the periodic table have the same:

explanation.body: Shared valence-electron count is why a group shows similar chemistry.

subject: chemistry
body: Down a group, metallic character generally:

explanation.body: Larger atoms lose electrons more easily, so metallic character rises down a group.

subject: chemistry
body: The modern periodic law states that properties of elements are a periodic function of their:

explanation.body: Moseley's revision replaced atomic mass with atomic number.

subject: chemistry
body: The bond formed by the transfer of electrons from one atom to another is:

explanation.body: Electron transfer produces ions held together electrostatically — an ionic bond.

subject: chemistry
body: The shape of a methane (CH$_4$) molecule is:

explanation.body: Four bonding pairs, no lone pairs on C: $sp^3$, bond angle $109.5^\circ$.

subject: chemistry
body: Which molecule is non-polar despite having polar bonds?

explanation.body: CO$_2$ is linear, so the two bond dipoles cancel; the others are bent or pyramidal.

subject: chemistry
body: The number of lone pairs on the central atom in water is:

explanation.body: Oxygen has 6 valence electrons; two form bonds to H, leaving two lone pairs.

subject: chemistry
body: According to VSEPR theory, a molecule with the general formula AB$_3$ and one lone pair on A has the shape:

explanation.body: Four electron domains (3 bonds + 1 lone pair) → pyramidal molecular shape, as in NH$_3$.

subject: chemistry
body: A coordinate (dative) covalent bond differs from an ordinary covalent bond in that:

explanation.body: In a dative bond one atom supplies the whole shared pair, e.g. NH$_4^+$.

options.body: both shared electrons come from one atom

subject: chemistry
body: For an exothermic reaction, the sign of $\Delta H$ is:

explanation.body: Heat is released, so the enthalpy of the products is lower — $\Delta H < 0$.

subject: chemistry
body: For a reaction at $300\ \text{K}$, $\Delta H = -100\ \text{kJ/mol}$ and $\Delta S = -200\ \text{J/(mol K)}$. Find $\Delta G$ in kJ/mol.

explanation.body: $\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S = -100 - 300(-0.2) = -100 + 60 = -40\ \text{kJ/mol}$.

subject: chemistry
body: A spontaneous process at constant temperature and pressure requires:

explanation.body: The sign of the Gibbs free-energy change decides spontaneity at constant $T,P$.

subject: chemistry
body: Which is a state function?

explanation.body: Enthalpy depends only on the state; heat and work are path-dependent.

subject: chemistry
body: Hess's law is a direct consequence of the fact that:

explanation.body: Because $\Delta H$ depends only on initial and final states, it is the same by any route.

subject: chemistry
body: The standard enthalpy of formation of an element in its most stable form is:

explanation.body: By definition, e.g. $\Delta H_f^\circ(\text{O}_2, g) = 0$.

subject: chemistry
body: For the reaction $\text{N}_2 + 3\text{H}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3$, increasing the pressure shifts the equilibrium:

explanation.body: Higher pressure favours the side with fewer gas moles (2 vs 4) — the product side.

subject: chemistry
body: The pH of a $0.01\ \text{M}$ solution of a strong monobasic acid (HCl) is:

subject: chemistry
body: Adding a catalyst to a reaction at equilibrium:

explanation.body: A catalyst speeds up forward and reverse rates equally; it only shortens the time to reach equilibrium.

options.body: does not change the position of equilibrium

subject: chemistry
body: For an endothermic reaction at equilibrium, raising the temperature:

explanation.body: Heat acts as a reactant; more heat drives the reaction forward, raising $K$.

subject: chemistry
body: The conjugate base of the ammonium ion NH$_4^+$ is:

explanation.body: Removing one H$^+$ from NH$_4^+$ gives NH$_3$.

subject: chemistry
body: A buffer solution resists changes in pH because it contains:

explanation.body: The weak-acid/conjugate-base pair neutralises added acid or base.

options.body: a weak acid and its conjugate base (or vice versa)
a strong acid and a strong base

subject: chemistry
body: Oxidation is defined as:

explanation.body: "OIL RIG": Oxidation Is Loss, Reduction Is Gain (of electrons).

subject: chemistry
body: The oxidation number of sulfur in sulfuric acid, H$_2$SO$_4$, is:

subject: chemistry
body: In the reaction $\text{Zn} + \text{Cu}^{2+} \rightarrow \text{Zn}^{2+} + \text{Cu}$, the oxidising agent is:

explanation.body: Cu$^{2+}$ is reduced (gains electrons), so it oxidises the zinc — it is the oxidising agent.

subject: chemistry
body: The oxidation state of oxygen in hydrogen peroxide, H$_2$O$_2$, is:

explanation.body: Peroxides are the standard exception: each O is $-1$.

subject: chemistry
body: A disproportionation reaction is one in which the same species is:

explanation.body: e.g. $\text{Cl}_2 + 2\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{Cl}^- + \text{ClO}^- + \text{H}_2\text{O}$: chlorine goes to both $-1$ and $+1$.

subject: chemistry
body: The sum of oxidation numbers of all atoms in a neutral compound is:

explanation.body: For a polyatomic ion it equals the ion's charge; for a neutral compound it is zero.

options.body: equal to the number of atoms

subject: maths
body: The sum of the roots of $x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0$ is:

explanation.body: For $x^2 + bx + c = 0$, sum of roots $= -b = 5$.

subject: maths
body: For what value of $k$ does $x^2 + kx + 9 = 0$ have equal roots (take the positive value)?

explanation.body: Discriminant $k^2 - 36 = 0 \Rightarrow k = \pm 6$; the positive value is $6$.

subject: maths
body: If the roots of $x^2 - px + q = 0$ are $2$ and $3$, then $(p, q)$ is:

explanation.body: Sum $= p = 5$, product $= q = 6$.

subject: maths
body: The quadratic $2x^2 + 3x + 5 = 0$ has:

explanation.body: Discriminant $= 9 - 40 = -31 < 0$, so the roots are a complex conjugate pair.

options.body: one real and one complex root

subject: maths
body: If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the roots of $x^2 - 6x + 4 = 0$, then $\alpha^2 + \beta^2$ equals:

explanation.body: $\alpha^2+\beta^2 = (\alpha+\beta)^2 - 2\alpha\beta = 36 - 8 = 28$.

subject: maths
body: One root of $x^2 - 7x + 12 = 0$ is $3$. Find the other root.

explanation.body: Product of roots $= 12$, so the other root is $12/3 = 4$.

subject: maths
body: The value of $i^{10}$ is:

subject: maths
body: Find the modulus of the complex number $3 + 4i$.

subject: maths
body: The conjugate of $\dfrac{1}{2 - i}$ is:

explanation.body: $\frac{1}{2-i} = \frac{2+i}{5}$; its conjugate is $\frac{2-i}{5}$.

subject: maths
body: If $z = 1 + i$, then $z^2$ equals:

subject: maths
body: The complex number $-1 + i\sqrt{3}$ in polar form has argument:

explanation.body: It lies in the second quadrant; reference angle $\arctan(\sqrt3) = \pi/3$, so argument $= \pi - \pi/3 = 2\pi/3$.

subject: maths
body: The sum $1 + i + i^2 + i^3$ equals:

subject: maths
body: Find the 10th term of the arithmetic progression $3, 7, 11, \dots$

subject: maths
body: Find the sum of the first 20 natural numbers.

subject: maths
body: The sum to infinity of the geometric series $1 + \tfrac12 + \tfrac14 + \dots$ is:

subject: maths
body: The geometric mean of $4$ and $9$ is:

explanation.body: GM $= \sqrt{4 \times 9} = \sqrt{36} = 6$.

subject: maths
body: The third term of a GP is $12$ and the sixth term is $96$. Find the common ratio.

subject: maths
body: If $a, b, c$ are in arithmetic progression then $2b$ equals:

explanation.body: The middle term is the average of its neighbours: $b = (a+c)/2$.

subject: maths
body: The value of $\sin 30^\circ + \cos 60^\circ$ is:

explanation.body: $\tfrac12 + \tfrac12 = 1$.

subject: maths
body: If $\tan\theta = \tfrac34$ and $\theta$ is acute, then $\sin\theta$ equals:

explanation.body: Right triangle with opposite $3$, adjacent $4$, hypotenuse $5$: $\sin\theta = 3/5$.

subject: maths
body: Convert $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ radians to degrees.

explanation.body: $\frac{\pi}{3} \times \frac{180}{\pi} = 60^\circ$.

subject: maths
body: The identity $1 + \tan^2\theta$ equals:

explanation.body: Dividing $\sin^2 + \cos^2 = 1$ by $\cos^2\theta$.

subject: maths
body: The general solution of $\sin\theta = 0$ is:

explanation.body: Sine vanishes exactly at integer multiples of $\pi$.

subject: maths
body: Find the maximum value of $3\sin x + 4\cos x$.

explanation.body: Maximum of $a\sin x + b\cos x$ is $\sqrt{a^2 + b^2} = \sqrt{9 + 16} = 5$.

subject: maths
body: The slope of the line $2x + 3y = 6$ is:

explanation.body: Rewrite as $y = -\tfrac23 x + 2$.

subject: maths
body: Find the distance between the points $(1, 2)$ and $(4, 6)$.

subject: maths
body: Two lines are perpendicular if the product of their slopes is:

explanation.body: $m_1 m_2 = -1$ for perpendicular lines (neither vertical).

subject: maths
body: The equation of the line through $(0, 3)$ with slope $2$ is:

explanation.body: Slope-intercept form with $m = 2$, $c = 3$.

subject: maths
body: Find the perpendicular distance from the origin to the line $3x + 4y = 10$.

subject: maths
body: The midpoint of the segment joining $(-2, 5)$ and $(4, -1)$ is:

subject: maths
body: Evaluate $\displaystyle\lim_{x \to 2} (x^2 + 3x - 1)$.

explanation.body: The polynomial is continuous, so substitute: $4 + 6 - 1 = 9$.

subject: maths
body: $\displaystyle\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{\sin x}{x}$ equals:

explanation.body: A standard limit.

subject: maths
body: Evaluate $\displaystyle\lim_{x \to 3} \dfrac{x^2 - 9}{x - 3}$.

explanation.body: Factor: $\frac{(x-3)(x+3)}{x-3} = x + 3 \to 6$.

subject: maths
body: The function $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{x}$ is discontinuous at:

explanation.body: It is undefined at $x = 0$ and continuous everywhere else.

subject: maths
body: $\displaystyle\lim_{x \to \infty} \dfrac{3x^2 + 2x}{x^2 - 1}$ equals:

explanation.body: Ratio of leading coefficients of equal-degree polynomials.

subject: maths
body: For $f$ to be continuous at $x = a$, we require $\lim_{x \to a} f(x)$ to exist and:

explanation.body: Continuity: the limit exists, $f(a)$ is defined, and the two are equal.

subject: maths
body: A fair die is rolled once. The probability of getting an even number is:

explanation.body: Favourable outcomes $\{2, 4, 6\}$ out of $6$.

subject: maths
body: Two fair coins are tossed. What is the probability of getting exactly one head? Give the answer as a decimal.

explanation.body: Outcomes HT and TH out of four equally likely: $2/4 = 0.5$.

subject: maths
body: If $P(A) = 0.6$, $P(B) = 0.5$ and $P(A \cap B) = 0.3$, then $P(A \cup B)$ is:

subject: maths
body: Events $A$ and $B$ are independent with $P(A) = 0.4$, $P(B) = 0.5$. Then $P(A \cap B)$ is:

explanation.body: For independent events, $P(A \cap B) = P(A)\,P(B) = 0.2$.

subject: maths
body: A bag has 3 red and 2 green balls. Two are drawn without replacement. What is the probability both are red? Give the answer as a fraction reduced to a decimal.

subject: maths
body: The probability of an impossible event is:

explanation.body: By definition; a certain event has probability $1$.

subject: biology
body: Which organelle is called the "powerhouse of the cell"?

explanation.body: Mitochondria carry out aerobic respiration, producing most of the cell's ATP.

subject: biology
body: A feature present in plant cells but absent in animal cells is:

explanation.body: Plant cells have a cellulose cell wall outside the membrane; animal cells do not.

subject: biology
body: Prokaryotic cells lack:

explanation.body: In prokaryotes the genetic material lies free in the cytoplasm (nucleoid); there is no nuclear envelope.

subject: biology
body: The site of protein synthesis in a cell is the:

explanation.body: Ribosomes translate mRNA into polypeptides.

subject: biology
body: The fluid-mosaic model describes the structure of the:

explanation.body: Singer and Nicolson's model: proteins floating in a fluid phospholipid bilayer.

subject: biology
body: Which organelle is involved in packaging and secretion of materials?

explanation.body: The Golgi apparatus modifies, sorts and packages proteins and lipids for secretion.

subject: biology
body: Lysosomes are known as "suicide bags" because they contain:

explanation.body: Rupture releases hydrolases that can digest the cell's own contents.

subject: biology
body: The monomer unit of a protein is:

explanation.body: Proteins are polymers of amino acids joined by peptide bonds.

subject: biology
body: Glycogen is the storage form of glucose in:

explanation.body: Plants store glucose as starch; animals store it as glycogen.

subject: biology
body: The bond that links two amino acids in a protein is the:

explanation.body: A peptide bond forms between the carboxyl of one amino acid and the amino group of the next, with loss of water.

subject: biology
body: Enzymes are biological catalysts that are chemically:

explanation.body: Almost all enzymes are proteins (a few RNA molecules, ribozymes, also catalyse reactions).

subject: biology
body: The secondary structure of a protein (α-helix, β-pleated sheet) is stabilised mainly by:

explanation.body: Hydrogen bonds between backbone C=O and N–H groups hold the helix and sheet together.

subject: biology
body: Which of these is a nitrogenous base found in RNA but not in DNA?

explanation.body: RNA uses uracil in place of DNA's thymine.

subject: biology
body: Fats and oils belong to which class of biomolecules?

explanation.body: Triglycerides (fats and oils) are lipids — esters of glycerol and fatty acids.

subject: biology
body: The green pigment that traps light energy for photosynthesis is:

explanation.body: Chlorophyll a is the primary photosynthetic pigment.

subject: biology
body: The loss of water vapour from the aerial parts of a plant, mainly through stomata, is called:

explanation.body: Transpiration is stomatal water loss; it drives the ascent of sap.

subject: biology
body: In C$_3$ plants, the first stable product of carbon fixation is:

explanation.body: RuBisCO fixes CO$_2$ onto RuBP, immediately splitting into two molecules of 3-PGA.

subject: biology
body: The plant hormone that promotes cell elongation and is involved in phototropism is:

explanation.body: Auxin redistributes to the shaded side of a shoot, causing it to bend towards light.

subject: biology
body: Water moves into a plant root hair cell by osmosis when the soil solution is:

explanation.body: Water moves from higher water potential (dilute soil solution) to lower water potential (cell sap).

options.body: more dilute than the cell sap
more concentrated than the cell sap

subject: biology
body: The opening and closing of stomata is directly controlled by:

explanation.body: When guard cells take up water and become turgid, the pore opens; when they lose water, it closes.

subject: biology
body: The functional unit of the kidney is the:

explanation.body: Each nephron filters blood and forms urine; a human kidney has about a million of them.

subject: biology
body: Exchange of gases between blood and air in the lungs occurs across the:

explanation.body: The thin-walled alveoli provide a huge surface area for gas exchange.

subject: biology
body: Which chamber of the human heart pumps oxygenated blood to the whole body?

explanation.body: The thick-walled left ventricle drives blood into the aorta and systemic circulation.

subject: biology
body: The enzyme in saliva that begins the digestion of starch is:

explanation.body: Salivary amylase (ptyalin) hydrolyses starch to maltose in the mouth.

subject: biology
body: Most reabsorption of glucose from the glomerular filtrate occurs in the:

explanation.body: The PCT reabsorbs essentially all filtered glucose, amino acids, and most water and ions.

subject: biology
body: The pigment in red blood cells that carries oxygen is:

explanation.body: Haemoglobin binds O$_2$ reversibly at its iron-containing haem groups.

subject: biology
body: Insulin, which lowers blood glucose, is secreted by the:

explanation.body: The pancreatic islet β-cells release insulin; α-cells release glucagon.

options.body: β-cells of the islets of Langerhans

subject: biology
body: An organism with two identical alleles for a gene is said to be:

explanation.body: Homo- = same; hetero- = different alleles.

subject: biology
body: A cross between two heterozygotes (Tt × Tt) gives an expected phenotypic ratio of:

explanation.body: Monohybrid cross: 3 dominant : 1 recessive phenotype (genotypes are 1 : 2 : 1).

subject: biology
body: Mendel's law of segregation states that:

explanation.body: Each gamete receives only one allele of each gene.

options.body: genes on the same chromosome always stay together
the two alleles of a gene separate during gamete formation

subject: biology
body: In humans, a male's sex-chromosome genotype is:

explanation.body: Females are XX; the father's sperm (X or Y) determines the child's sex.

subject: biology
body: A colour-blind man marries a woman homozygous for normal vision. Their sons will be:

explanation.body: Sons get their X from the mother (all normal); daughters become carriers.

subject: biology
body: The ABO blood group system in humans is an example of:

explanation.body: Three alleles ($I^A$, $I^B$, $i$) exist in the population, though any individual has only two.

subject: biology
body: The theory of evolution by natural selection was proposed by:

explanation.body: Darwin (with Wallace) set it out in "On the Origin of Species" (1859).

subject: biology
body: Homologous organs (e.g. the forelimbs of a human, whale and bat) provide evidence for:

explanation.body: Same basic structure, different functions — descent with modification.

options.body: divergent evolution from a common ancestor

subject: biology
body: The wings of an insect and the wings of a bird are:

explanation.body: Same function (flight), different origin — an example of convergent evolution.

subject: biology
body: According to the Hardy–Weinberg principle, allele frequencies in a population stay constant in the absence of:

explanation.body: The principle holds only when none of those five evolutionary forces acts.

options.body: mutation, migration, selection, genetic drift and non-random mating

subject: biology
body: Industrial melanism in the peppered moth is a classic example of:

explanation.body: Soot-darkened trees favoured dark moths; the environment selected for the melanic form.

subject: biology
body: The earliest forms of life on Earth are thought to have been:

explanation.body: Life arose before free oxygen accumulated, so the first cells were anaerobic prokaryotes.

subject: biology
body: Organisms that make their own food from inorganic raw materials are called:

explanation.body: Green plants and some bacteria fix carbon, forming the base of the food chain.

subject: biology
body: In a food chain, roughly what percentage of energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next?

explanation.body: The "10 percent law" of Lindeman: most energy is lost as heat at each step.

subject: biology
body: Fungi and bacteria that break down dead organic matter are:

explanation.body: Decomposers recycle nutrients back into the ecosystem.

subject: biology
body: The pyramid of energy in an ecosystem is always:

explanation.body: Because energy is lost at each transfer, each level holds less than the one below — the pyramid never inverts.

subject: biology
body: The process by which atmospheric nitrogen is converted into a form usable by plants is:

explanation.body: Nitrogen-fixing bacteria (e.g. Rhizobium) convert N$_2$ into ammonia/nitrate.

subject: biology
body: A group of organisms of the same species living in a given area is a:

explanation.body: Population = one species; community = all interacting populations in the area.
